fixes.title: Flat wizard cannot capture a flat when a filter move is needed - its wheel move neither takes effect nor is confirmed, while the same move works from Equipment
fixes.summary: Two halves of one cause: nothing refreshes filterWheelStateProvider after a bare filterWheelSetPosition. (1) The settle loop in FlatWizardNotifier.moveFilterWheelAndWait polled ref.read(filterWheelStateProvider) while nothing in the loop fetched status, so the provider could never change and EVERY move timed out at 15 s even though the driver had completed it. The loop now re-reads getFilterWheelStatus from the backend each pass and pushes position/moving back into the provider, exactly like its working counterpart DeviceService._verifyFilterWheelPosition (control_helpers.dart:294-330). (2) The verifier's escalation - 'the stale state also makes the NEXT run unsafe: my second run skipped the move and exposed seven frames labelled Ha while the driver sat on position 3' - came from the early `if (!fwState.isMoving && fwState.currentPosition == position) return null;` shortcut, which trusted the same never-refreshed cache. That shortcut now confirms the position from the DEVICE before deciding the move can be skipped; an unreadable status is logged and falls through to commanding the move rather than being read as 'already there'. Cause confirmed in native: api_filterwheel_set_position (bridge/src/api/devices/simulation.rs:1215) calls mgr.filter_wheel_set_position directly and publishes NO FilterChanging/FilterChanged event, unlike unified_device_ops.rs:1092-1133 - so any caller that does not poll afterwards leaves the provider stale (the headless /filterwheel/position endpoint the web dashboard uses, apps/desktop/lib/headless_api/handlers/device_handlers/filter_wheel_handlers.dart:44, is one such caller and is now survivable).
fixes.test: cd packages/skotiq_core && flutter test test/providers/flat_wizard_workflow_hardening_test.dart -> 10/10 pass (2 new: 'a completed move is confirmed from the DEVICE, not from a provider nothing refreshes' and 'a provider that wrongly claims the wheel is already on target does NOT skip the move'). Both drive the fake wheel ONLY through the backend (backend.wheelPosition) and never poke the provider, which is the production shape.
fixes.revert_check: Two separate reverts, both confirmed. (a) Severed the settle loop's production call site - replaced the whole `final status = await deviceBackend.getFilterWheelStatus(fwState.deviceId!); ... fwNotifier.updatePosition/setMoving ...` block with the original `final reachedTarget = live.currentPosition == position; if (!live.isMoving && reachedTarget) return null;`: 3 tests failed ('capture waits for the filter wheel to STOP MOVING before exposing' -> saveCount 0 not 1; both new tests -> 'filter wheel did not confirm position 1 within 2s' instead of null). (b) Restored the cached shortcut `if (!fwState.isMoving && fwState.currentPosition == position) return null;` in place of the device confirm: 'a provider that wrongly claims the wheel is already on target does NOT skip the move' failed (backend.wheelMoves was [] - the move was skipped). Restored -> 10/10 pass.
fixes.caveats: I deliberately did NOT take the finding's other proposed half - 'emit a position-changed event from the filter wheel driver after a successful set'. Emitting FilterChanged the instant mgr.filter_wheel_set_position returns would tell every UI listener the wheel has SETTLED, which is not knowable for an async wheel; that is the same 'the app states something untrue' class this campaign is hunting, and it cannot be validated here (no cargo build). Polling the device, as DeviceService already does, is the honest fix and needs no native change.
